svg.title: Agentic Shiksha architecture image set
svg.desc: Five Agentic Shiksha architecture views using flat cards, dashed groups, and colours sampled from the project logo. Official Microsoft product icons appear beside the corresponding service names, with their original colours and proportions preserved. The separate palette key does not add workload nodes or connections.

svg.title: Agentic Shiksha: Platform ecosystem
svg.desc: Layered view of learner, teacher and administrator experiences, agent capabilities, application runtime and managed data services. Layers group capabilities; they are not individual microservices. The teacher dashboard is embedded in the main web app. Graph memory is an optional path, detailed in figure 05. Source snapshot: 30 SEP 2026. Not a live deployment inventory.

g.text: A course-grounded teaching and learning platform, from experience to infrastructure.

g.data-card: TA harness / context, tools and turn lifecycle
g.text: TA harness / context, tools and turn lifecycle

g.data-card: FastAPI / sessions, courses, artifacts and progress
g.text: FastAPI / sessions, courses, artifacts and progress
Capability layers, not deployment units. See 02 for service ownership and 05 for opt-in learner memory.

svg.title: Agentic Shiksha: Service architecture
svg.desc: Main React frontend and FastAPI backend, separate admin React frontend and FastAPI backend, and their shared managed dependencies. The admin UI also calls the main API for course placement and assignments. The admin API is not a proxy. Its access boundary must be independently authenticated and restricted; this figure is not a security-completeness claim. Source snapshot: 30 SEP 2026. Not a live deployment inventory.

g.text: Four independently built services, with explicit ownership of user experiences and APIs.
Learner chat / course builder / embedded teacher dashboard
Sessions / course access / chat / teacher routes
TA harness / material and curriculum workers
Four independent builds. Teacher views use the main API; the admin API is not a proxy for it.

svg.title: Agentic Shiksha: Teaching-agent runtime
svg.desc: A learner turn passes user and course checks, enters the canonical TA harness, exchanges turns with a named Foundry agent, uses learning tools and streams results to React. SSE and AG-UI are transport adapters, not separate agents. Tool results return to the same agent turn. Graph-memory context is only injected under the configured authoritative policy. Source snapshot: 30 SEP 2026. Not a live deployment inventory.

g.text: One course-specific TA turn: trusted context, agent execution, tools and streamed learning artifacts.
Active-user and course checks / answer depth / optional image and artifact context

g.data-card: SSE / AG-UI > React chat, artifacts and saved conversation state
g.text: SSE / AG-UI > React chat, artifacts and saved conversation state
Tools return results to the same agent turn. SSE and AG-UI are delivery contracts, not separate agents.

svg.title: Agentic Shiksha: Course and knowledge pipeline
svg.desc: Explicit teacher submission starts persisted jobs. Source documents go to Blob Storage, a layout and embedding pipeline and Azure AI Search. Course creation registers a Foundry TA and enqueues curriculum work. Course Companion proposes unsaved form edits; it does not submit Create or Update. TA creation, material indexing and curriculum readiness are tracked separately. Search is course grounding, not a learner mastery store. Source snapshot: 30 SEP 2026. Not a live deployment inventory.

g.text: Teacher-owned course setup becomes searchable materials, a named TA and a versioned curriculum.
Course Companion proposes form edits; the teacher chooses when to submit.
Hybrid keyword + vector retrieval / semantic reranking
TA creation, material indexing and curriculum have separate readiness states; a created TA is not a ready course.

svg.title: Agentic Shiksha: Learner memory and evidence
svg.desc: A reviewed curriculum graph and policies constrain event processing. Durable learner events produce evidence and validated observations, followed by a deterministic reducer, an atomic snapshot and derived learning views. Disabled by default. Course modes are off, shadow and authoritative. Shadow writes evidence without becoming progress authority; authoritative mode supplies TA context and learning-state authority. Cosmos stores graph documents; no separate graph database is required. Hosted memory and legacy progress are not the evidence ledger. Source snapshot: 30 SEP 2026. Not a live deployment inventory.

g.text: Opt-in graph memory: shared curriculum definitions, separate learner facts and evidence-backed state.
Authorized views; TA context and state authority in authoritative mode

g.data-card: LLM proposes observations. Policy decides state.
g.text: LLM proposes observations. Policy decides state.
Cosmos document storage / private evidence in Blob / no separate graph database
Modes: off / shadow / authoritative. Hosted recollections and legacy progress are not the evidence ledger.
Sampled from the Agentic Shiksha logo.
Service logos retain their official colours.
Colours indicate emphasis, not deployment status.
